thread.title: Apple Stock Gets Price-Target Cut On iPhone Weakness

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Stock Gets Price-Target Cut On iPhone Weakness
text:
Investment bank Morgan Stanley on Friday turned cautious on Apple ( AAPL ) ahead of its March-quarter report. It lowered its price target on Apple stock, citing weaker iPhone sales.
X Apple shares plunged 4.1% to close at 165.72 on the stock market today , tumbling through their 50-day moving average and approaching the 200-day line. The iPhone maker retreated 2.8% on Thursday after Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ( TSM ), which makes chips for Apple, warned of weaker smartphone demand.
Apple's sell-off spurred a retreat in the broader stock market, with the S&P 500 index, Nasdaq composite and Dow Jones industrial average all undercutting their 50-day lines intraday.
Analyst Katy Huberty reiterated her overweight rating on Apple, but trimmed her price target to 200 from 203. In a note to clients, she advised investors to buy shares on any weakness after the company's fiscal second-quarter results on May 1. She remains positive on the stock due to Apple's improving capital return outlook and services growth.
Meanwhile, investment research boutique OTR Global lowered its rating on Apple stock to mixed from positive, according to Seeking Alpha . OTR Global said the iPhone is losing ground in China to local competitors.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Downside Seen Morgan Stanley's Huberty expects Apple to report in-line results for the March quarter, but sees a big downside to current consensus estimates for the June quarter following iPhone production cuts and China sales weakness.
"We believe the June-quarter consensus iPhone shipment estimate of 42.9 million (units) could be revised meaningfully lower to account for weak supply chain data points and continued weakness in China data," she said.
Huberty lowered her June-quarter iPhone shipment estimate to 34 million units, down from 40.5 million. She is modeling for earnings per share of $1.80 on sales of $46.2 billion in the June quarter, vs. consensus estimates for $2.18 and $52.1 billion.
Apple Capital Return Plan Huberty predicts Apple will increase its total capital return program by $150 billion when it reports. That would bring its cumulative total to $450 billion for share buybacks and dividends, expiring in March 2020.
Expectations for a step-up in capital returns likely are embedded in Apple's current valuation, she said. That could result in a "sell the news" reaction from investors on May 1, Huberty said.
